extracted.intended_audience: British Parliamentarians and the politically engaged public (18th-century Britain)
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and evaluative standards for national administration, colonial policy, commercial regulation, and foreign negotiation; aimed at judging ministers' conduct and the soundness of public measures. Emphasizes evidence, consultation with stakeholders, administrative unity, and the primacy of trade over revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of the right to levy colonial money
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific power of levying money in the colonies must be retained as a sacred trust in the hands of Great Britain; without it 'the presiding authority of Great Britain...would vanish into an empty name.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This power should be reserved not primarily for ordinary supply but as a final means of control; surrendering it would dissolve unity and subordination in the empire. Political reconciliation may differ from legal speculation; policy must reflect human nature rather than pure reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base parliamentary decisions on full evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Founding repeal or major measures on the whole detail of affairs laid before Parliament: every paper of office and pertinent testimony should be placed before the Houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignorance misleads Parliament; knowledge alone brings it into the right road. Use exhaustive documentary and witness evidence (civil and military officers, revenue officers, merchants, manufacturers) to inform legislative judgment rather than relying on confident assertions or ministerial promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give due weight to merchant and manufacturer testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Merchants' and manufacturers' depositions about debts, trade stoppage, discharged artificers, and mercantile credit were necessary to present the situation vividly to Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat their testimony seriously when they report concrete economic consequences of policy (unpaid debts, suspended justice, seizure risks). Disregarding such testimony risks ignoring the practical effects of measures; contrarian hypothetical testimony would be implausible and rightly distrusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize trade over revenue in colonial policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Take trade as the primary end and revenue as a very subordinate consideration: when trade is likely to suffer, prefer protecting commerce to extracting taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-makers should prefer measures that preserve channels of commerce even if they reduce immediate tax yield, because the long-term benefits of trade outweigh contemptible revenue returns. This principle guided commercial/regulatory decisions in the administration under defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit revenue measures to the object and collection realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Suit the revenue to the object; keep duties balanced with the risk of smuggling and the difficulty of collection in the colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating excessive temptations to smuggling by keeping duties proportionate to collection capacity. Tailor duties to local circumstances to minimize evasion and increase actual collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target commercial restrictions narrowly where the problem exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply restraints specifically to the parts of commerce where clandestine or harmful trade exists rather than imposing indiscriminate limits on colonial commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlarge allowable foreign trade for colonies where possible without harming the mother country, and confine restrictive measures to the actual loci of injury (e.g., ports, routes) to secure returns while expanding beneficial exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult a broad and representative set of commercial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform commercial policy by convening merchants and manufacturers from all considerable towns, and confer publicly rather than rely on a few favorites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid decisions driven by flattery, private contracts, or a narrow clique. Use numerous, public meetings and wide geographic representation so trade's unanimous opinion can guide regulation. Beware of relying solely on partisan pamphlets or the author's own assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use merchant expertise in foreign-negotiation advice
rubrics_metrics.description: In treaties and foreign commercial negotiations, consult merchants resident and active in the relevant foreign courts; their approbation is crucial evidence of the treaty's practical value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior instructions and steps should conform to merchant opinion; local merchant endorsement (e.g., 'entire and unreserved approbation of every article') is strong practical evidence in favor of negotiated terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise rigor and persistence in pursuing legitimate foreign claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims such as the Manilla ransom or Canada bills should be pursued vigorously, even if previously neglected; lack of earlier vigor complicates later negotiation but is not a reason to abandon the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revive and press just claims upon foreign courts energetically; avoid tacit abandonment. Changes in administration should not be used as an excuse for prior remissness; sustained diplomatic effort can lead to arbitration or favorable settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure demolition or enforcement of treaty obligations abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: When treaty obligations (e.g., demolition of Dunkirk jetties) are at stake, actively inspect and press for performance rather than acquiescing to ongoing violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers should personally survey problems when necessary, remonstrate, and, where appropriate, insist on corrective measures rather than tolerating construction or obstruction that violates prior agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form cohesive administrations based on mutual trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Major offices of deliberation and execution should be held by those who can trust one another; a united administration secures the predominance of right and uniform principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for administrations where the principal ministers can deliberate and execute with confidence and fidelity. While perfect unity is impractical, approaching that standard reduces the contagion of distrust and disconnection; incoherent coalitions carrying unreconciled discord will not be 'healing coalitions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate leaders by constancy and independence from faction
rubrics_metrics.description: The test of who is fit to 'restore us to health' is whether men are free from factional attachments and can adhere to consistent principles, not the vague claim of 'men of ability and virtue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish sound from tainted politicians by their willingness to abandon principles for coalition or personal advancement. True worth is shown by steadfast adherence to the public good even when that means foregoing immediate advancement or spoils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency in punishment and reward to preserve public morals
rubrics_metrics.description: It is futile to check irreligion and licentiousness by punishing one individual if others equally culpable are rewarded with honors and emoluments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions and honors should be applied consistently; perceived partiality erodes public and private faith and undermines the moral authority of the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ministerial appointments that create venal dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware of appointments and contract arrangements that make merchants or others dependent on ministerial favor, leading to private advantage over the general good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject systems that reward private advantage through favoritism; ensure that those advising or benefiting from policy do so in ways aligned with the general good of trade and the nation rather than personal profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer practical, tested measures over partisan self-praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not celebrate regulatory schemes as 'prodigies of wisdom' without demonstrating their beneficial tendency by independent authorities or affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy claims should be validated by the judgment of those most affected (e.g., merchants, manufacturers) rather than by circular appeals to partisan pamphlets or internal pamphlet-to-pamphlet citation.
